breaking.headline: Sanofi to buy Insmed for $41 billion in cash
breaking.fact: Sanofi agreed Tuesday to buy U.S. biotech Insmed for $41 billion in cash at $175 a share, a 17% premium to Monday's close — the biggest biotech deal in nearly three years. Insmed shares jumped 14% premarket and Sanofi rose about 5%. The deal gives Sanofi two commercial respiratory drugs as its blockbuster Dupixent nears patent expiry.

breaking.headline: Futures slip as Nvidia gives back some of Monday's record rally
breaking.fact: Wall Street futures slipped on Tuesday as chip stocks cooled after Monday's historic rally, with Nasdaq futures down about 1% and S&P futures off 0.3%. Nvidia fell 4-5% premarket, giving back part of its record 31% surge, while Micron, AMD and Marvell dropped 3-4%. Investors now await Wednesday's inflation data before the Fed's December meeting.

breaking.headline: Houston added 25,000 jobs in October, double the usual pace
breaking.fact: The Houston area added nearly 25,000 jobs in October, more than double the usual amount for the month, according to a new Workforce Solutions report. The gain followed a weak September and keeps Houston's job growth ahead of the state's pace. Texas added 30,600 jobs statewide in October.

breaking.headline: Virginia and Oregon sue Musk's SpaceX over Grok deepfakes
breaking.fact: Virginia and Oregon sued Elon Musk's SpaceX on Monday over Grok, alleging the AI chatbot's 'spicy mode' generated millions of sexualised images — including more than 20,000 depicting children — from ordinary photos. The states, the first to sue, seek damages and court orders under consumer-protection law. SpaceX, which Sean holds via SPCX, has not commented.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide edged up 0.04% in Paris to €187.66, worth $205.28 at the ECB's Nov 23 reference rate of 1.0939. The industrial-gas giant sat out Monday's historic U.S. rally, its defensive profile on full display while tech names soared. The euro sparkline shows a slow, orderly drift with no break in either direction. With no company news in play, the dollar price from here mostly tracks the euro's moves.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic slipped 1.43% to $87.64 on Monday, drifting back toward its $83 IPO price after the debut pop. The AI name gave back ground even as the broader market staged its best day since April, and it was trading lower again in Tuesday's premarket. The listing is barely a week old, so the tape is still finding its level. Watch whether $83 holds as the first real test of IPO support.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL ticked up 0.01% to $91.60, its usual penny-a-day grind as the Treasury bill ETF accrues interest. The fund keeps paying its monthly distribution — $0.30849 per share, ex Nov 2, paid Nov 5 — and the distribution yield sits at 4.04%. It is the quiet corner of the watchlist: no drama, just steady Treasury income. With the Fed now seen hiking again in December, short rates stay the story here.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet jumped 6.34% to $282.10 on Monday, riding the AI relief rally after Nvidia's Jensen Huang returned as CEO. The move clawed back most of last week's slide, though the stock is still well below its autumn highs near $320. Search and cloud momentum remain the fundamental story, with AI infrastructure spending the swing factor. Tuesday's premarket cooling bears watching after such a sharp one-day run.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly rose 1.30% to $1,364.60 on Monday, a steady gain on a day the market rewarded almost everything. The drugmaker keeps grinding higher on GLP-1 demand and its deep pipeline, with the Sanofi-Insmed $41 billion deal putting a spotlight on pharma valuations. Lilly is now one of the market's largest names by value. Watch for any read-through from the biotech deal wave to Lilly's own deal appetite.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere Energy added 0.21% to $295.46, a quiet session while crude slid to three-month lows on recovering supply. The LNG exporter is insulated from day-to-day oil swings by its long-term contracts, but gas prices and export demand set the tone. With winter demand season approaching and global LNG trade shifting, volumes matter more than the oil tape. The stock remains near the top of its recent range.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia rocketed 31.48% to $165.05 on Monday after the board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, adding about $952 billion in value — the largest one-day gain ever for a U.S. company. The stock gave back 4-5% in Tuesday's premarket as traders banked gains. The SEC probe, the California review and Huang's Dec 1 House testimony are still open. Sean's call stands: long-term hold until the probes shake out.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer was flat at $27.40 on Monday, sitting out the rally even as pharma made headlines. Sanofi's $41 billion cash deal for Insmed — $175 a share, a 17% premium — put biotech valuations in focus, and Pfizer's own pipeline and dividend remain the story. The stock has drifted lower for weeks and needs a catalyst of its own. Any sector deal wave could put Pfizer's deal-making back on the table.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab surged 9.27% to $49.63 on Monday, bouncing hard with the risk-on rally after sliding for a week. The space name had fallen from above $61 to $45.42 on Friday before Monday's snapback, so the move looks like relief as much as conviction. Launch cadence and the Neutron program remain the fundamental drivers. Watch whether the bounce holds above $50 or fades with the broader chip-led cooling.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital gained 1.37% to $8.16 on Monday, a modest rise on a huge market day. The mortgage REIT keeps paying its dividend while rates stay high — the 10-year Treasury sits near 4.92% — and its servicing portfolio benefits when refinancing stays slow. The stock has traded in a tight band for weeks. The December Fed meeting, where a hike is now priced as near-certain, is the next real catalyst.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SpaceX rose 4.35% to $133.35 on Monday with the broad rally, but a legal cloud arrived after the close: Virginia and Oregon sued SpaceX on Monday over Grok's sexualised images, the first states to sue. The suits seek damages and court orders under consumer-protection law. SpaceX has not commented. The Starship program, meanwhile, is quiet until Ship 43's static fire in mid-December.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist Financial climbed 2.36% to $46.89 on Monday, joining the broad bank rally as the market snapped back. Regional banks benefit when recession fears ease, and Monday's 4.7% S&P surge did just that. The stock has been rebuilding from its autumn lows with the dividend intact. Watch the December Fed decision — a hike would lift net interest margins but could also slow loan demand.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony jumped 7.17% to $2.39 on Monday, one of the day's sharpest watchlist moves. The bottom watch fired on both UAMY and UEC at Monday's close, the agreed tripwire, and the watch re-arms from Tuesday. Antimony's critical-mineral status and any Defense Department contracting news remain the catalysts. The stock is still far below its autumn highs, so this looks like an oversold bounce so far.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy surged 10.19% to $5.84 on Monday, bouncing off Friday's $5.30 low as the bottom watch fired on the close. The uranium name had been beaten down with the AI-led selloff, and Monday's snapback was the strongest in weeks. Nuclear expansion and government uranium buying remain the long-term thesis. Watch whether the bounce extends or fades with Tuesday's cooler premarket tone.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero fell 1.43% to $329.40 on Monday, one of the few watchlist names in the red as crude slid to three-month lows. Brent settled at $89.37 and WTI at $80.17 as recovering Gulf supply and Libya's Sharara restart outweighed Hormuz tensions. Refiners feel lower crude through margins, not just prices. Valero has now given back a chunk of its autumn gains and sits well below its $419 highs.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Target Retirement 2035 fund rose to a $28.51 NAV on Monday, up 2.74% from Friday's $27.75 as stocks staged their best day since April. The balanced fund's equity sleeve did the heavy lifting while its bond holdings steadied the ride. It is the set-and-forget core of the watchlist, rebalancing itself as 2035 approaches. The December Fed meeting is the next event that could move its bond side.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: The S&P 500-anchored estimate puts VI5TC at $148.76, up 4.73% with Monday's historic index rally. The estimator tracks the S&P 500's move from its Nov 3 anchor, and Sean's own check put it within about 0.1% of the real price. The fund's actual holdings are index-linked, so the estimate moves tick-for-tick with the market. Tuesday's softer futures suggest a small give-back at the open.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money fund holds its $1.00 NAV with a 7-day SEC yield of 3.78%, published Nov 23 by Schwab. The sweep vehicle keeps shrinking as Sean moves balances over $1,000 into CDs, per the November plan to wind it down. The inherited-IRA slice is exempt from the nudge until March. With a December Fed hike now priced as near-certain, money-fund yields may edge up rather than down.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money fund holds its $1.00 NAV with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.03%, published Nov 23 by Vanguard. It remains the top-yielding cash on the watchlist and the parking spot for the ANT proceeds and the Seiver Slough and Lodge sale streams in the income model. The fund owns only Treasuries, so it carries no credit risk. A December Fed hike would likely lift its yield further.

weekInBrief.headline: Asia roars back as Huang's return revives the AI trade
weekInBrief.body: Asian stocks roared back on Tuesday as Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia revived the AI trade. Japan's Nikkei added 4.5%, South Korea's Kospi surged 7.5% and Taiwan's market jumped 9.1%, with TSMC up nearly 10%. The rebound came a day after Tokyo had slid 5% on the same AI fears.

weekInBrief.headline: Fourteen countries back the ICJ genocide ruling on Myanmar
weekInBrief.body: Fourteen countries, including the UK, Canada and Australia, formally acknowledged the International Court of Justice's ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017. Britain separately said it would formally recognise the genocide and sanctioned five senior Myanmar military figures. The court ruled on Nov 19 that the 2017 crackdown in Rakhine state was genocide.

weekInBrief.headline: Texas pitches Houston as home of the U.S. Space Academy
weekInBrief.body: Texas has formally proposed Houston as the home of the proposed United States Space Academy, the Texas Space Commission announced. The plan leans on Johnson Space Center, the Texas A&M Space Institute and Houston Spaceport, with groundbreaking targeted by 2027 and first classes in 2028. Ohio and Florida are competing for the NASA-led academy, and no site has been selected.

weekInBrief.headline: Delta outage delayed 1,000-plus flights at the start of Thanksgiving week
weekInBrief.body: Delta Air Lines resolved an automation outage on Sunday that delayed more than 1,000 flights nationwide at the start of Thanksgiving travel week. The system that calculates aircraft weight and balance failed, forcing manual workarounds and a brief ground delay at Atlanta, Delta's main hub. Lingering delays stretched into Monday as millions of Americans began holiday travel.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed late Monday that three oil tankers hit naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz while sailing under U.S. Navy escort, a claim that has not been independently verified — no vessels have been named and U.S. Central Command has not responded. The Joint Maritime Information Center kept the threat level at 'severe,' warning further attacks are 'highly likely' after recording seven tanker attacks between Nov. 16 and 21, the most since the war began in February. The U.S. is also eyeing Iran as a possible culprit in dozens of new cyberattacks against ships, the Wall Street Journal reported.

space.headline: Euclid finds the most distant quasar ever — 630 million years after the Big Bang
space.body: ESA's Euclid telescope has found the most distant quasar known, J1504+6252, nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. The quasar, the first found beyond redshift 8, is powered by a black hole about 360 million times the Sun's mass. Follow-up with Hubble and the James Webb telescope confirmed the find, published today in Astronomy & Astrophysics.

space.headline: FDA approves the first-ever treatment for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy
space.body: The FDA on Monday approved Welgemda (ribitol), the first medicine for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, a rare inherited disease that weakens muscles and can impair breathing. The oral drug, from BridgeBio, showed improved walking speed and lung function in its phase 3 trial. BridgeBio expects an immediate U.S. launch.

space.headline: A galactic shock wave may rewrite the map of the Milky Way
space.body: A University of Sydney study in Nature Astronomy finds the Milky Way's central bar drives shock fronts through gas clouds that trigger star formation — unusual, since bar shocks normally suppress it. The work suggests part of the so-called Norma spiral arm may not be an arm at all, but star formation along the bar's leading edge. The bar is estimated at about 14,000 light-years long.

space.headline: A clock that ticks through two times at once may soon be testable
space.body: Physicists have worked out how today's ultra-precise trapped-ion atomic clocks could detect a clock experiencing two flows of time at once, a quantum effect where motion exists in superposition. The framework, published in Physical Review Letters, boosts sensitivity to the effect by up to 1,000 times. The effect itself has not yet been observed — building the experiment is the next step.

apod.title: Galaxies Battle in the NGC 7771 Group
apod.explanation: After this galaxy battle, only one galaxy will remain. Already visible in the featured picture are rings and faint star swirls from previous gravitational encounters. Known collectively as the NGC 7771 Group, these galaxies lie almost 200 million light-years away toward the constellation Pegasus. The largest galaxy, barred spiral NGC 7771 on the lower right, is itself about 75,000 light-years across, and the galaxy on the upper left is spiral NGC 7769, which is almost as large. As these and other smaller galaxies make repeated close passages, they will all likely merge into one very large galaxy.
